c’est un film très lent, avec une atmosphère étrange et de très très très très longs dialogues. c’est un infini procès, avec une embrouille interminable, qui révèle une ambiance très sombre et des personnages tous plus bizarres les uns que les autres. on comprend pas tout et c’est très compliqué d’accrocher. certains plans sont filmées de façon original, et les scènes sont vraiment longues. c’est un film chargé en émotion, avec beaucoup de secrets enfouies. au bout d’un moment ça devient vraiment interminable, des faits surgissent, des hypothèses sont conjecturées, mais c’est jamais explicitement concret. bon ok la façon dont c’est réalisé est très intéressante. par contre, j’ai carrément détesté la fin, pcq tout le long on s’attend à une réponse concrète mais le but du film c’est justement de ne donner aucune réponse, du coup c’est super frustrant. toute l’histoire on peut l’interpréter seulement par des « peut être » et jamais par de véritables faits. chacun des personnages sont intéressants, avec des points de vus différents et des façons de subir la situation différentes, mais le spectateur est à la place des jurés, donc c’est très compliqué de savoir démêlé le vrai du faux. le film rappelle que le verdict ne coïncide pas forcément avec la vérité, et les hypothèses de la potentielle vérité restent plausible. cependant le lien avec le titre du film est très pertinent, en montrant la chute de chacun des personnages de façon disséquées. bon, en toute honnêteté je n’ai pas aimé. le fond du film est émouvant et bien recherché. MAIS, c’est lent + dialogues interminables + bcp de choses abstraites et surtout surtout surtout le film répond à rien, ça te laisse sur ta fin, c’est à toi d’interpréter et de trouver la vérité, la fin est ouverte et ne répond à aucune questions que tu te poses durant tout le film. c’est frustrant et c’est carrément ce que je n’aime pas.

[I]t’s both a product and an echo of high-minded consensus. It’s a movie of manifest ambition, suggested by the literary milieu in which it’s set and the themes that come with it, but one that realizes its ambition with prefabricated attitudes and a numbingly conventional form that only reinforces them. It’s prestige cinema... As the cinematic equivalent of an airport read, Anatomy of a Fall is adequate—not brisk but twisty, not stylish but unobtrusively informational. Richard Brody in The New Yorker Ouch!!! But also: fair enough. Brody's judgement on this film coincides with mine completely. To me, it's one of the most mystifyingly overrated films in contemporary history. This mid-range did she/didn't she drama, bolstered by remarkable performances but nevertheless bland and utterly conventional in execution - this was considered by the Cannes jury  to be the very best that world cinema had to offer in 2023? Did none of them imagine what someone like Hitchcock or Michael Mann would have done with the same material? Brody compares the film unfavourably with Alice Diop's Sant Omer , which by coincidence was a toss-up with this film for our Sunday afternoon watch. Finally the prestige attached to a Cannes Golden Palm winner and the considerable reputation of Sandra Hüller whom we remember so fondly from The White Ribbon Toni Erdmann , Across the Aisle and The Zone of Interest won out. Don't say these tokens of cinema prestige have no effect on viewing choices... Brody goes on to imagine a curious would-be young cinephile lured into watching Anatomy precisely because of its selection as Cannes winner, and thus the representative of the finest cinematic art: I imagine the bewilderment that would follow the viewing—imagine it developing into a skepticism, or even wrath, that would risk engulfing far better films, ones also endorsed at the same festivals and hailed by the same notables. If this is the art of the movies, I imagine hearing, then movie art is bullshit. In the art-house consensus, the danger facing contemporary cinema is its artistic diminution brought about by the market dominance of commercially ravenous franchise films. The showcasing and enshrining of mediocre movies as masterworks poses as great a danger. More ouch! But also... more 'fair enough, if you think about it'. The thing about this movie isn't that it's bad - if only it had the courage to be bad - but that it's utterly and completely uninteresting. If anyone other than Sandra Hüller had been in the lead it would have tanked as another dull Euro-melodrama about bo-bos (bourgeois bohemians) of the type that Michael Haneke so successfully torpedoed in Caché . Again, I invite the viewer to imagine what Hitchcock, or Mann - or to go closer to home, taking French women directors only as our reference, Alice Diop or Claire Denis - would have done with this scenario of an ambiguous death subject to jury trial. In the case of Hitchcock there would have been texture of some kind at the very least, and in the case of Claire Denis a commitment to the physicality of violent death . In other cases (imagining here French directors Emmanuel Marre and Julie Lecoustre, of Zero Fucks Given ) there would have been an authorial point of view of some kind, taking in class politics, feminism, colonialism, xenophobia, the justice system... anything except this... nothing at all, this dull directorial detachment. Brody outlines the moment he knew that this would not be an interesting watch: There’s the revelation that Sandra is bisexual, which, as I watched the movie, struck me as an instant exoneration, for the simple reason that a film governed by high-minded consensus would no longer dare to posit a bisexual woman as a wanton killer; the same goes for the fact that Sandra is the more productive and successful writer, and that she’s a foreigner. There’s the prosecuting attorney’s buzzcut, suggesting that he’s a right-wing bigot who takes all these clues and identifiers as suspicious. He’s a perfect embodiment of traditionalist persecution of a sexually and intellectually free woman artist (and of a foreigner)... In short, Anatomy of a Fall is a movie of prefabricated attitudes, and its dramatic construction is airtight and incurious to match. It's a far cry from condemning a movie as "woke" - whatever that might mean - to say that its absolute conformity to conventional consensus attitudes robs it of any real tension. It's not so much a question of acceptable or unacceptable viewpoints, or of correct or incorrect opinions, so much as that ambiguity, the essence of such a mystery "thriller", and certainly of the courtroom variety, needs to thrive in the doubtful spaces. An absurdly aggressive skinhead prosecutor and a bisexual foreign woman set up a dynamic in which there is only one possible answer. [ASIDE: It's like, when Barack Obama recommends some book or film, I immediately determine to avoid it - not because it has ideas I disagree with, but by virtue of the fact that Obama has enjoyed it, I already know what it's about and what will happen. I'll probably agree with it all the way through, to the point of utter boredom. Blandness like that ('Obama-Brain') is its own value, separate in its absolute insipid quality from the ongoing woke vs antiwoke kerfuffle, which interests me not one jot.] Which makes it all rather absurd to see the fuss and faff that director Justine Triet has made surrounding the ongoing "mystery" of the formally unresolved death (unresolved, that is, in cinematic terms, not in legal terms - Sandra has been exonerated in court, but no directorial intervention establishes her innocence within the text of the film). On set, Hüller repeatedly asked Triet whether her character was guilty or not, but the director refused to answer. Triet ended up instructing Hüller to play her character as innocent, which Triet later said was "very sneaky", since Hüller did not have an answer. When a journalist asked Triet at the Golden Globe Awards press room in January 2024 if Sandra did kill her husband, Triet replied: "I will tell you in 10 years." Wikipedia on Anatomy of a Fall Oh please! I'm not going to interrupt my duties in 2034, scavenging in the blasted sun-drenched radioactive streets amid the heat-resistant cockroaches for scraps of nourishment, in order to roll up to Justine Triet in her luxury bomb shelter and ask about whether Sandra Hüller killed her hubbie in some movie we've all forgotten about. I already know the answer, Justine: please don't try to fake a mischievous subtext to a story that is, so boringly, simply a plain and overt text about a mystery that becomes a big nothing.

Mettez du respect et de la lumière sur le cinéma féminin. Un film de procès qui ne cherche jamais vraiment le verdict, mais la faille. Triet construit son récit comme une dissection minutieuse du couple, où chaque certitude s'effrite à mesure que le tribunal (et le spectateur) croit avancer. Sandra Hüller y est habitée d'une opacité fascinante : on ne sait jamais si son intelligence est une armure ou un aveu. Mais au-delà du dispositif judiciaire, c'est une question bien plus vertigineuse que pose le film : connaît-on vraiment l'autre ? Son voisin, son frère, sa sœur, son ou sa compagne ? Aucune famille n'échappe aux secrets de polichinelle, à ces zones d'ombre qui persistent sans jamais être nommées. Chaque foyer a ses casseroles, ses non-dits tolérés en silence. C'est ce qui rend le film aussi dramatique que profondément humain. Il ne s'agit pas de juger un couple, mais de mesurer combien la connaissance intime de l'autre [ et de soi-même ] reste toujours partielle, négociée, parfois illusoire. Une leçon d'humilité face à la complexité des êtres. La mise en scène, souvent austère, presque clinique, épouse cette froideur alpine du chalet, comme si le décor lui-même refusait de trancher. C'est là toute l'ambiguïté du film : il ne raconte pas une mort mais l'impossibilité de connaître véritablement l'autre même après des années de vie commune. Les 2h30 pèsent par moments, notamment dans les longueurs procédurales qui, même si elles nourrissent le vertige du doute, testent aussi la patience. L'usage de l'anglais, pivot thématique plus que coquetterie, dérange certains. J'avoue que j'ai eu du mal avec ce yoyo entre les langues mais c'est à tort selon moi, tant il matérialise la distance entre les langues, les cultures, et finalement entre les personnes elles-mêmes. Une Palme d'or qui ne fait pas l'unanimité, et c'est peut-être normal. le film refuse lui-même toute unanimité sur ce qu'il raconte comme il refuse toute certitude sur ceux qu'on croit connaître. Pas le meilleur rythme mais très bon film.

Derrière son apparence de film judiciaire se cache avant tout une dissection fascinante d’un couple en crise, où chaque détail du quotidien prend une importance capitale. Le suspense autour de ce whodunit atypique fonctionne parfaitement, mais le véritable sujet est ailleurs : les ressentis, les incompréhensions et les visions opposées que deux personnes peuvent avoir d’une même histoire. Sandra Hüller livre une prestation remarquable, parvenant à transmettre une multitude d’émotions d’un simple regard. Une réalisation subtile qui nous plonge au plus près des émotions des personnages. Un très bon film.

Best Criterion purchase I made since Memories of Murder . ________________________________________________________ Anatomy of a Fall enticed me from the premise alone. A woman is blamed for her husband’s death and the only witness is her blind son. That in it of itself is enough to get my attention. The film is an amazing courtroom drama. It’s similar to A Few Good Men in that every single court sequence is riveting, filled with incredible dialogue and tense confrontations. The movie does a great job creating suspense and tension. I genuinely did not know how it was all gonna play out. What makes this movie stand out though is at its heart, it’s a family drama. It’s about a marriage on the brink of collapse, and how the couple’s issues are impacting their loved ones. It tackles very real topics like infidelity, sexuality, childhood, abuse, depression, and grief. I found myself caring about these characters and the struggles they endured throughout the movie’s runtime. Everything about this movie felt real. Never once did I feel like I was watching a movie. Anatomy of a Fall felt more like someone hid a camera inside someone’s house rather than actors reciting lines from a script (a very well written script I might add) in front of a camera. The authenticity of this film is thanks equally to the screen writer(s) and the actors. Sandra Hüller in particular is downright incredible. The realism of this movie is a bit of a blessing and a curse. I love that the director allowed certain scenes to “breathe.” It created a bunch of heartfelt moments and it gives the viewer the chance to sit with these characters and empathize with them. That being said, I felt like some scenes dragged on for a little too long, and it ruined the pacing in some parts. But once again, maybe on second watch, I’ll feel differently. Bottom line, I love Anatomy of a Fall . I can’t wait to watch it again. In fact I kinda have to watch it again. I watched it while my wife was at book club. When she returned and realized I was watching this movie, she was like “OMG I wanted to watch that too!” Sorry babe. 😜

bir köpek var filmde, hani al tüm oyunculuk ödüllerini ona ver inanılmaz iyi oynamış. Bir sabaha açılıyor film, bir aile. Anne, baba ve çocuk. Çocuğumuz görme engelli, Annemiz sahnede son derece sıcak fakat babamız öyle mesafeli ki kadraja girmeye bile yeltenmiyor. Sadece açtığı müziğin sesiyle varlığından haberdar ediyor bizi. Bu tanıtımdan sonra, bir düşüş gerçekleşiyor. Çocuğumuz evde değilken, baba pencereden düşüp ölüyor. O sırada evde bulunan tek kişi olan Anne ise ileride gerçekleşecek duruşmaların baş şüphelisi konumuna geçiyor. Daha sonra, filmimiz ilerledikçe bu düşüşü derinlemesine analiz ediyor, bir bakıma anatomisini çıkarıyor. Bu düşüş yalnızca  ölüme yol açmış bu kaza/cinayetin değil; bir aşkın, bir ailenin ve en önemlisi kişilere dair kafamızda oluşturduğumuz portrelerin de düşüşü. Onlara atfettiğimiz her bir iyi özelliğin, birlikte yaşadığımız her bir güzel anının bambaşka bir bağlamda nasıl bir silaha, korkunç bir eylemin kanıtına dönüşebileceğinin anatomisi. İşte bu film, tam olarak bununla ilgileniyor. İki saat otuz dakika boyunca filmimiz bunu anlatıyor. Gerçekte ne oldu? Aslında daha doğrusu, gerçekte ne olduğunu düşünüyorsun? Bu soru, izleyiciye düzenli olarak soruluyor ve  verdiğimiz cevaplar çoğu zaman (en azından benim verdiğim) bir öncekinden farklı oluyor. Spoiler olmayacak merak etmeyin, sadece ufak bir sahneden örnek vermek istiyorum. Bana kalırsa film başlangıçta sıkıca annemizin perspektifinden ilerliyor. Ortam onun açısından kuruluyor, onun gözlerinden şahit oluyoruz. Haliyle çoğumuz bu davada Annemin tarafını tutmuş oluyor. Sonra duruşmalar başlıyor ve bir sabah bir ses kaydı dinliyoruz. Ses kaydı bir tartışma hakkında. Önce ufak gerginlikler çıkıyor, sonra saygının sürdürüldüğü bir tartışmaya dönüyor. Fakat ne zamanki bu tartışma fiziksel şiddetin de dahil olduğu bir kavgaya dönüyor, görüntü kesiliyor ve aynı karakterlerimiz gibi sadece ses kaydıyla tanık oluyoruz geçmişe. Burada artık ne olduğunun kararı bize düşüyor. Ve o ana kadar her zaman tek bir açıya güvenmiş olan biz, kendimizi şüphe ederken buluyoruz. Film, bu tarafsız anlatımını soğuk atmosferi ve karakterlere mesafeli duruşuyla güçlendirmiş. Aynı zamanda ara ara kameranın el çekimi, handheld bir tarza geçmesiyle de sizi olan olayların içine bırakıyor. Kimi zaman kamera yaşananlara ayak uyduramıyor, sahne pozlamasında hatalara yer veriyor ve olanları olduğu gibi sergilemekte başarısız oluyor. Bu sayede anlattığı temayı da ustalıkla desteklemiş oluyor. Oyunculuklar gerçekten de efsane. Yazdığım birçok incelemede oyunculukları övüyorum, ben de bunun farkındayım. Fakat bana sorsanız en iyi oyunculuklar hangi filmdeydi diye, şüphe bile etmeden Anatomy of a Fall derdim. Sandra Hüller, kendi ana dili olmayan iki dilde konuşmasına rağmen destansı bir performans vermiş. Milo Machado-Graner unutulmaz bir oyunculuk sergilemiş. Hem çocuk oyuncu, hem görme engelli bir karakter hem de yas sürecini anlatan senaryo. Aktörümüz aleyhine olabilecek tüm durumların üstesinden ustalıkla gelmiş. Kadrodaki diğer oyuncularsa ortalamın çok üstünde performanslar vererek bu iki başrolümüzün emeğini boşa çıkarmamış. Son olarak, filmi sıkıcı bulan insanların olduğunun farkındayım. Hatta bunlardan birisi ablam. Dürüst konuşmam gerekirse beni bir an bile sıkmadı. Hatta film beni içine almakta o kadar başarılıydı ki bir sahnede karakterin sigarasından gelen dumanın benim odamda dolaştığını sandım. Zevk meselesidir diyip filmin temposu hakkındaki kararı size bırakıyorum. Benim için kusursuza çok yakın bir filmdi. Duygusal bağ kurmakta zorlanmış olsam da bunun bir sonraki izleyişimlerimde gerçekleşebileceğine hâlâ daha inanıyorum. Ayrıca, bir noktada bu duruma bilerek yapıldığını düşündüğümden çok da büyük bir problem olarak bakamıyorum. Şiddetle tavsiye ediyorum.
